correctness.rationale: For \(n\ge3\) and arbitrary nonnegative \(q\), each shared color is forced onto a single deleted matched pair by graph adjacency. Every coloring has a unique decomposition into paired shared colors and two disjoint exclusive palettes. The open-neighborhood uniqueness criterion is equivalent to singleton persistence under all one-element punctures; its \(s=0\), \(s=1\), and \(s\ge2\) cases are exhaustive and disjoint, with a necessary all-doubleton exception in \(s=0\). Partial Bell coefficients count precisely the surjective shore colorings. Combinatorial multiplication and summation give the exact full polynomial. The four-color case is derived analytically by exhausting s. Independently, exhaustive direct checks of 28,666,423 maps on 14 profiles match the formula, and recurrence checks through \(n=12\) match the classification. No finite check substitutes for the uniform proof.

originality.rationale: The exact all-palette proper conflict-free coloring polynomial and the complete four-color rigidity/exceptional-order census are mathematically stronger than the known scalar chromatic-number result. The closest previously public crown-graph work states the color-sharing lemma and minimal number of colors but explicitly does not classify all optimal colorings. The new theorem classifies the punctured multiset singleton obstruction for arbitrary palette sizes, accounting also for all-doubleton configurations. Relevant complexity, ordinary proper-coloring, and complete-multipartite results do not imply this counting polynomial. No equivalent full count was identified in published-finding corpus, or targeted external literature searches; this is not proof that all possible unpublished or unindexed work was excluded.
residual_risks: A differently phrased or unindexed paper might already contain the exact enumeration or an equivalent general theorem.
Relevant 2026 PCF decision/computational research was assessed from abstracts, not fully inspected; its titles and claims are less directly relevant than the completely read crown-graph theorem.
The polynomial uses a class-size summation; it is exact but not simplified into a single closed-form product.

value.rationale: The complete polynomial is a natural exact enumerative invariant that refines the recently studied PCF decision/minimum-color problem on an infinite classical dense bipartite family. The all-doubleton loophole is an intrinsic structural feature of punctured color multisets, not a free parameter choice. In optimal four-colorings the classification changes sharply: order four has three types and 384 labeled maps, while every larger order has one structural type and 24 binomial(n,2) maps. This is a complete classification, supplies all higher-palette counts, and provides reproducible exact independent census checks without overclaiming a general graph counting theorem.
